scope: Frozen optimized compact-interface Codex A/B experiment on 40 fresh synthetic task IDs.
conclusion: No measured token, execution-time, local-resource or coding-success advantage versus standard Codex on this corpus. Actual monetary benefit remains unavailable.

causes_and_hypotheses.finding: Every B attempt performs one successful compact fetch_context; A performs no MCP calls. B indexing adds a mean 0.207526 seconds, whereas its matched Codex+index gap averages 4.881461 seconds.
causes_and_hypotheses.limit: Indexing alone cannot explain the entire observed time gap; no randomized component ablation assigns the remainder.

causes_and_hypotheses.finding: B increases total input by 32.82%, cached input by 40.27%, output by 5.31%, and uncached input by 2.17% overall. Individual and subgroup uncached-input results are mixed.
causes_and_hypotheses.limit: The native usage totals do not attribute tokens to schemas, history, returned source or reasoning.

causes_and_hypotheses.finding: Both arms pass 80/80 external graders; this corpus has a measured correctness ceiling. B increases sampled local CPU and peak process-tree RSS.
causes_and_hypotheses.limit: The experiment cannot establish a success advantage on harder tasks or long-lived memory use.

causes_and_hypotheses.finding: MCP connection startup, tool schemas, an extra model/tool interaction and overlapping context can exceed retrieval value on small purpose-built tasks.
causes_and_hypotheses.test: Run separate preregistered startup/schema/protocol/source-selection ablations on newly authored repositories with unchanged grading and cache-order controls.

causes_and_hypotheses.finding: Warm indexes or accepted prior memories may help related multi-step work more than an empty memory database on independent tasks.
causes_and_hypotheses.test: Evaluate controlled task sequences with explicit accepted memories, separate cold setup from recurring requests, and prevent oracle leakage.

proposed_next_steps.action: Investigate total token overhead before further default changes. Separate schema/startup/extra-round-trip effects from returned-source size using randomized ablations.
proposed_next_steps.gate: Use actual CLI input/cached/output, completion, timing and full cost coverage; preserve each failed or negative trial.

proposed_next_steps.action: Reduce overlapping source and metadata while preserving complete primary/helper bodies and visible freshness limits.
proposed_next_steps.gate: Judge body coverage, precision and safety on independent repositories; smaller bytes alone are insufficient.

proposed_next_steps.action: Evaluate warm project reuse and explicit accepted memories across related tasks.
proposed_next_steps.gate: Report cold setup and recurring overhead separately, with memory provenance and no hidden answer seeding.

proposed_next_steps.action: Broaden evaluation to larger unfamiliar repositories and harder tasks that avoid the observed 100% grade ceiling.
proposed_next_steps.gate: Freeze a new task corpus and protocol before model runs, include task-test and failure results, and repeat with counterbalanced ordering.

proposed_next_steps.action: Collect reliable provider charges or verified pricing before evaluating money.
proposed_next_steps.gate: Cost per success includes every attempted cost; label list-price calculations separately from invoiced charges.

limitations: Forty purpose-built synthetic task IDs across four repository families, with two repeats per configuration, are 160 attempts rather than 160 independent tasks. The corpus was not used for retrieval tuning or model development pilots, but it is not a sample of production repositories.

A and B share frozen model/settings/prompts/seed commits and workspace sandbox. The B treatment includes the compact protocol and its instructions, fresh indexing, MCP startup and retrieval; this combined experiment does not isolate individual mechanisms.

OS/provider caches cannot be reset. First-arm order reverses per task in repetition two, but cache mix, host/provider variability and repeated task exposure remain confounders. Subgroup results are descriptive and correlated.
Each B run has a fresh index, private session and database. This does not measure persistent cross-task or cross-process memory/history benefits.
CLI total input includes cached input. Cached input is a subset, not an additional amount. Derived uncached input is total minus cached after checking valid numeric bounds.

Actual provider invoiced cost and verified-price computed costs are unavailable. Cost per success must include costs for every attempt, including failures; both arms remain null despite 80 external successes each. ChatGPT authentication does not expose per-run invoiced cost.
Underlying model/API calls are unavailable. There are 160 task CLI invocations and 160 completed CLI turns; neither establishes the number of internal model requests.

The native stream contains 80 successful fetch_context calls in B and none in A. This establishes source-bearing treatment delivery, not reliance on the returned content or semantic completeness. Optional verify_context was never invoked, so its live model behavior is not measured here.

External graders test requested behavior, public-API cases where defined, protected files/metadata, unchanged smoke tests and TypeScript compilation. They do not prove arbitrary production correctness.

Completion rate uses external grader passes divided by all attempted runs. Invalid, failed, ungraded and not-run observations would remain visible; this campaign contains none. No retries or supplemental attempts were pooled.
Codex+index timing excludes worktree creation, independent post-exit audits, external grading and report writing. Preflight requests and old-task pilots are outside the160 task comparisons.

Local process CPU is a sampled lower bound; RSS can miss short-lived peaks and double-count shared pages. Memglide is already a subset of total process resources. Index setup CPU is parent-process only, and indexing peak RSS is unavailable.

The independent post-exit source hash comparison is a later point observation before grader mutations. Own edits can explain mismatches; matches do not reconstruct earlier call-time freshness or guarantee continuous freshness. Excluded non-source/unsafe files stay unknown.

Exact repeated filesystem reads are unavailable. Observed read-command counts are narrow intent proxies that omit internal/MCP/script/directory reads and are not guaranteed filesystem-I/O lower bounds.
Mean, median and nearest-rank p95, pair ratios and small strata are descriptive without confidence intervals or statistical significance claims.

Earlier V1 and development pilot results involve different prompts/protocols/corpora/source stages. Differences across those reports do not establish a causal optimization benefit; no historical run was replaced.

native_command_items.definition: Unique native command_execution items recorded in the supported CLI stream; command intent differs and this is not a model-call or filesystem-read count.
native_command_items.interpretation: Five fewer observed command items coexist with eighty additional MCP calls. The net difference is descriptive and does not attribute any command replacement to a particular tool call.

live_context_audit.declared_body_eligibility: Two symbols per task, judged against immutable starting Git blobs with Python AST or narrow TypeScript fixture scanner; returned file hash must match the starting blob. Repeated observations are correlated.
limitations: This is a post-experiment content audit of actual native MCP event results, not a model cost meter.
Target-file coverage is a declared-file proxy; expected declaration/body coverage is narrowly scoped to the two symbols declared by each synthetic task. Full semantic completeness is unknown.

Exact body checks use independent Python AST or the narrow TypeScript fixture scanner against immutable starting Git blobs. A check is eligible only when that returned file hash matches the starting blob; post-edit or unknown versions are not treated as missing baseline bodies.

Source versions recorded after Codex exit and before grading are later observations. A model's intended edits can cause mismatches; neither matches nor mismatches establish source freshness at the instant of retrieval.
Server status, source_freshness, truncation and warnings are application assertions. Independently verified live call-time freshness remains unavailable.
Native event ordering establishes only whether a completed retrieval preceded observable command starts. Commands may read or mutate source; the full filesystem history is not measured.
Snippet and canonical JSON bytes are measured response content, not transport bytes, tokenizer counts, model input tokens, or money saved.
Missing, interrupted, failed, ambiguous and ineligible observations remain visible and unknown; no unobserved responses are invented as zero-byte or successful retrievals.
A does not expose Memglide MCP and receives no invented retrieval-quality scores. Repeated runs and related tasks are correlated; this is a small synthetic corpus.
